sam-sales: FYI — Acme evaluation showing an odd gap in trace IDs when we stream logs to their Splunk forwarder. POC is on their RTX cluster. They also hit intermittent 429s from our log ingest endpoint. Can eng take a quick look?

matt-eng: @sam-sales can you paste a raw log line + the export config? 429s suggest rate limiting on our side or too-big batching.

sam-sales: here's an example line they sent (redacted):
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-19T15:02:10Z","level":"info","msg":"request complete","request_id":"req_123","user":"u-987"}
```
Note: `trace_id` missing, but Redwood console shows the trace for the same request. Suspect our export transform dropped `trace_id`.

rachel-sre: two quick Qs — are we doing prefix-trimming or log rotation that might drop `trace_id` in multiline parsers? Also, which export format are they using (syslog/HTTP JSON)?

sam-sales: they configured the Splunk forwarder to accept JSON via HTTP. We send batches of 100 by default. They said when they reduce batch_size to 10 the 429s stop, but then some trace_ids still missing.

matt-eng: can you share the `exporter` config? suspect either our batch JSON wrapper strips nested fields, or theirs flattens and loses nested `trace` object.

sam-sales: config snippet they sent:```yaml
exporter: splunk-http
batch_size: 100
format: json
flatten: true
```

matt-eng: ah — `flatten: true` likely collapses nested `trace.id` into `trace.id` key that their parser rejects. That could cause the missing `trace_id` in Splunk search. Also 429s mean we need backoff.

rachel-sre: immediate mitigation: set `batch_size: 10` and `flatten: false` on their forwarder. We'll also add 429-aware retry with exponential backoff in our exporter. I can push a quick canary change to POC route.

opsbot: Deploy started for canary export-backoff @eng-runtime — build #4128

matt-eng: great. For root cause, please capture an exported payload showing the `trace` structure before and after transform. If they can paste one request that appears in console but missing in Splunk that would help.

sam-sales: asked them for the failing examples. They provided one where our console shows `trace_id: tr-abc` but Splunk shows nothing. Sending now:
```
Console view: { request_id: "req_123", trace: { id: "tr-abc", span: "s1" } }
Export payload (post-transform): { request_id: "req_123", trace.id: "tr-abc" }
```

rachel-sre: yep — their Splunk HEC likely rejects keys with dots unless told. Two paths: set `flatten:false` or map `trace.id` => `trace_id` in transform. I'll add a quick field-mapper in canary.

matt-eng: also adding 429 handling: reduce concurrency and exponential backoff for 429/503. Can we add metrics so we can see per-tenant 429 spikes in Console?

rachel-sre: yes — I'll add a per-tenant 429 counter + last-failure-sample to the POC metrics dashboard. Sam, tell the customer we have a canary patch rolling and recommended config until it's live: `batch_size: 10, flatten: false` or map `trace.id` -> `trace_id`.

sam-sales: sending guidance now. They prefer mapping to `trace_id` because they don't want nested fields. Can we include a quick transform snippet they can drop into forwarder?

matt-eng: send this:```json
{ "mappings": [ { "from": "trace.id", "to": "trace_id" }, { "from": "trace.span", "to": "span_id" } ] }
```

sam-sales: shared it. Customer applied mapping and reports trace ids now appear in Splunk. They still saw a couple of 429s during spikes; will monitor after we ship the backoff canary.

rachel-sre: canary deployed. opsbot: Deploy complete for canary export-backoff build #4128 to p-poc-eu1.

opsbot: Deploy success — 2 instances healthy.

matt-eng: follow-up actions: 1) prod-ify transform mapper (+ docs), 2) expose per-tenant 429 metric in Console, 3) add recommended Splunk forwarder configs to POC playbook.

sam-sales: thanks team — customer pleased with quick turnaround. Closing this swarm unless we see recurring spikes. :thumbsup:
